easy.def: To bring things or people together.
examples: We gather sticks for the fire.
We gather around the campfire.
Hens gather by the food.

more.def: To collect things into one place, or to come together as a group.
examples: The class gathered around the teacher to hear the story.
Squirrels gather nuts for the winter.
A crowd gathered to watch the street performer.
It was generous of you to share your snack.
The generous girl gave me half her snack.
My aunt is generous with hugs.

more.def: Willing to give time, money, or help to others freely.
examples: Our generous neighbor gave vegetables from her garden to everyone on the street.
He was generous with his time and helped every student.
A generous gift helped the town build a new playground.
Be gentle with the baby.
The gentle horse let me pet it.
Use a gentle voice in the library.

more.def: Kind, calm, and careful; not rough or strong.
examples: A gentle rain fell on the garden all morning.
The nurse was gentle when she cleaned the cut.
A gentle breeze moved the leaves.
The dinosaur was gigantic.
A gigantic rock sat on the hill.
We saw a gigantic ship.
A gigantic balloon floated over the parade.
The redwood trees in the forest are gigantic.
The baker made a gigantic cake for the town party.
I glance at the clock.
She glanced at me and smiled.
I glance out the window.

more.def: To look at something quickly and then look away.
examples: She glanced at her watch to check the time.
The driver glanced in the mirror before changing lanes.
He glanced over the menu and ordered quickly.
It is a gloomy, rainy day.
The cave was gloomy.
He felt gloomy when his friend left.

more.def: Dark and dull, or feeling sad and without hope.
examples: The gloomy old house had not seen sunlight in years.
Everyone felt gloomy after the team lost the final game.
The sky was gloomy all week, with no sign of the sun.

easy.def: To give off a soft light.
examples: My night-light glows in the dark.
The stars glow at night.
The fire glows red.

more.def: To shine with a soft, steady light.
examples: The campfire glowed long after the flames died down.
Fireflies glowed in the dark field.
Her face glowed with happiness.

easy.def: Something you want to do and work hard for.
examples: My goal is to read ten books.
I kicked the ball to score a goal.
His goal is to learn to swim.

more.def: Something you are trying to reach or achieve.
examples: Her goal is to learn to play the violin this year.
Our class goal is to collect five hundred cans of food.
He set a goal to save enough money for a bike.
I am grateful for my family.
I am grateful for your help.
We are grateful for the sunny day.

more.def: Feeling or showing thanks for something good.
examples: We were grateful to the neighbors who helped us move.
The lost hikers were grateful to see the rescue team.
She wrote a note to say how grateful she was for the gift.

easy.def: What pulls things down to the ground.
examples: Gravity makes the ball fall down.
Gravity keeps us on the ground.
Without gravity, we would float.

more.def: The force that pulls objects toward the Earth and keeps us on the ground.
examples: Because of gravity, a dropped pencil always falls to the floor.
Gravity pulls the rain down from the clouds.
There is less gravity on the moon than on Earth.
The greedy boy took all the cookies.
Do not be greedy. Take just one.
The greedy dog ate the cat's food too.

more.def: Wanting much more of something than you need or than is fair.
examples: The greedy king kept all the gold for himself.
The greedy pirate wanted all the treasure for himself.
It would be greedy to take more than your share.
I am grumpy when I am tired.
The grumpy man did not smile.
My cat is grumpy after a bath.

more.def: Easily annoyed and in a bad mood.
examples: He is always grumpy before he has eaten breakfast.
The grumpy troll would not let anyone cross the bridge.
She felt grumpy because she had slept badly.

easy.def: To give an answer when you are not sure.
examples: Can you guess what is in the box?
I guess you are six years old.
Guess which hand has the coin.

more.def: To give an answer or opinion without knowing for certain.
examples: I guessed that there were two hundred beans in the jar.
Can you guess the ending of the story?
I did not know the answer, so I had to guess.
The lights guide the ships.
Mom guides the baby's hand.
A map will guide us.

more.def: To lead or show the way to someone.
examples: A ranger guided us along the trail to the waterfall.
The stars guided sailors across the sea long ago.
A helper guided the new student to her classroom.
